steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: You may record multiple takes and submit your BEST performance — but each piece must be a single continuous take, not edited together.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Accompaniment can be live or backing track — the accompaniment level must not dominate your performance. Choose appropriate accompaniment for your genre.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Performance anxiety is normal — manage it through: thorough preparation, slow breathing, positive visualisation, and performing to others before the recording.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The teacher marks your performance against AQA criteria, then moderation adjusts the standard — consistency across the cohort is checked.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe how performance preparation and assessment are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use performance preparation and assessment. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use performance preparation and assessment in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their | A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how performance preparation and assessment are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using comp | A practical application showing understanding of how performance preparation and assessment can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intended

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use PRECISE musical vocabulary — not vague descriptions like it sounds nice Reference SPECIFIC musical elements when analysing any piece For listening questions: identify elements FIRST, then explain their effect For study pieces: know the context, structure and key features in detail For performing: focus on accuracy, expression and interpretation For composing: show development of ideas, not just repetition
